set.st: April 1964: two men admitted burgling $500 in coins from a Rochelle grocery and said they hid them in a pillowcase under a railroad bridge in town; the coins were gone when police looked. The burglars were two Rochelle men, 23 and 22; when police went to the spot, under a rock beneath the CB&Q railroad bridge, they found only the imprints of coins in the mud; the police chief thought children playing there had taken them. Pin is approximate, not the spot itself.

Rockford Register Star, 22 Apr 1964: 'the CB&Q railroad bridge'; the Burlington's Aurora-Savanna line crosses the Kyte River in Rochelle; bridge not yet fixed, pin stays on the town.
